wrong.en: gave would mean she gave the talk. “but she fell ill” shows it didn't happen.

tasks.prompt: Last month we ___ our prices, but our biggest client threatened to leave.

ok.de: „Last month“ und „but … threatened to leave“: ein Plan von damals, der nicht klappte → were going to.
ok.en: “Last month” plus “but … threatened to leave”: a past plan that fell through takes were going to.

wrong.de: are going to blickt von heute nach vorn. „Last month“ ist aber vorbei.
wrong.en: are going to looks ahead from today. But “Last month” is over.

wrong.de: will raise ist eine Aussage über die Zukunft. „Last month“ erzählt aber von einem Plan damals.
wrong.en: will raise is about the future. But “Last month” tells of a plan back then.

tasks.prompt: We ___ the lease when the landlord suddenly added a new clause.

ok.de: „when the landlord suddenly added“: Ihr wart kurz davor, dann kam etwas dazwischen. Dafür steht were about to + Grundform.
ok.en: “when the landlord suddenly added”: you were on the point of it, then something intervened. That takes were about to.

wrong.de: Nach about folgt to + Grundform: were about to sign, nicht about signing.
wrong.en: About is followed by to + base form: were about to sign, not about signing.

wrong.de: are about to steht in der Gegenwart. „added“ zeigt aber, dass alles in der Vergangenheit lag.
wrong.en: are about to is present. But “added” shows it all happened in the past.

tasks.prompt: The webinar ___ when our main speaker lost her internet connection.

ok.de: „when … lost her connection“: Der Start stand kurz bevor, dann passierte etwas. Dafür steht was about to.
ok.en: “when … lost her connection”: the start was moments away, then something happened. That takes was about to.

wrong.de: would erzählt, was später wirklich geschah. Hier stand der Start kurz bevor → was about to start.
wrong.en: would tells what really happened later. Here the start was moments away: was about to start.

wrong.de: is about to steht in der Gegenwart. „lost“ zeigt aber die Vergangenheit → was about to.
wrong.en: is about to is present. But “lost” shows the past, so use was about to.

tasks.prompt: Back in 2016, the startup hired a young engineer who ___ later design its best-selling product.

ok.de: „Back in 2016 … later“: Von einem Punkt in der Vergangenheit blickst du auf Späteres. Dafür steht would + Grundform.
ok.en: “Back in 2016 … later”: from a past point you look at something later. That takes would + base form.

wrong.de: will blickt von heute aus. Die Geschichte spielt „Back in 2016“, deshalb would.
wrong.en: will looks from today. The story is set “Back in 2016”, so use would.

wrong.de: had braucht ein Partizip (had designed). Vor der Grundform design steht would.
wrong.en: had needs a participle (had designed). Before the base form design, use would.

tasks.prompt: The two firms ___ merge in 2020, but the deal collapsed at the last minute.

ok.de: „but the deal collapsed“ zeigt: Es war damals fest geplant. Förmlich steht dafür were to + Grundform.
ok.en: “but the deal collapsed” shows it was firmly planned back then. Formally, that takes were to + base form.

wrong.de: Deutsch „sollten fusionieren“ verleitet zu should. should gibt aber einen Rat, keinen Plan von damals.
wrong.en: German “sollten fusionieren” suggests should. But should gives advice, not a past plan.

wrong.de: are to steht in der Gegenwart. „in 2020“ und „collapsed“ zeigen die Vergangenheit → were to.
wrong.en: are to is present. “in 2020” and “collapsed” show the past, so use were to.

tasks.prompt: The new system ___ live last spring, but testing took far longer than expected.

ok.de: „but testing took far longer“: Der Plan von damals klappte nicht. Das sagt was to have + Partizip.
ok.en: “but testing took far longer”: the plan back then fell through. That's what was to have + participle says.

wrong.de: should go klingt nach Rat für jetzt. „last spring“ verlangt einen Plan von damals → was to have gone.
wrong.en: should go sounds like advice for now. “last spring” needs a plan from back then: was to have gone.

wrong.de: will have gone blickt in die Zukunft. „last spring“ ist aber vorbei.
wrong.en: will have gone looks into the future. But “last spring” is over.

tasks.prompt: The client needs our signed offer ___ the end of the day, or the deal is off.

ok.de: „the end of the day“ ist eine Frist: spätestens dann fertig. Eine Frist steht mit by.
ok.en: “the end of the day” is a deadline: done by then at the latest. A deadline takes by.

wrong.de: Deutsch „bis“ verleitet zu until. until nennt aber eine Dauer. Für eine Frist steht by.
wrong.en: German “bis” suggests until. But until names a duration. A deadline takes by.

wrong.de: within steht vor einer Zeitspanne (within two days), nicht vor einem Zeitpunkt wie „the end of the day“.
wrong.en: within goes before a time span (within two days), not before a point like “the end of the day”.

tasks.prompt: The help desk stays closed ___ Monday morning, when the upgrade is finished.

ok.de: „stays closed“ ist ein Zustand, der ohne Pause andauert. Die Dauer bis zu einem Zeitpunkt steht mit until.
ok.en: “stays closed” is a state that lasts without a break. Duration up to a point takes until.

wrong.de: by nennt eine Frist für eine einmalige Handlung. „stays closed“ dauert aber an → until.
wrong.en: by sets a deadline for a one-off action. But “stays closed” lasts, so use until.

tasks.prompt: Under the new policy, every support ticket must get a reply ___ 24 hours of receipt.

ok.de: „24 hours of receipt“ ist eine Zeitspanne ab dem Eingang. Spätestens am Ende dieser Spanne: within.
ok.en: “24 hours of receipt” is a span from arrival. By the end of that span at the latest: within.

wrong.de: by steht vor einem Zeitpunkt (by Friday). Vor einer Zeitspanne wie „24 hours“ steht within.
wrong.en: by goes before a point in time (by Friday). Before a span like “24 hours”, use within.

wrong.de: in 24 hours meint den Zeitpunkt nach 24 Stunden. Mit „of receipt“ passt within.
wrong.en: in 24 hours means the point after 24 hours. With “of receipt”, use within.

tasks.prompt: ___ January 1, all travel bookings must go through the new portal.

ok.de: „January 1“ ist der Stichtag, ab dem die Regel gilt. Dafür steht as of.
ok.en: “January 1” is the key date from which the rule applies. That takes as of.

wrong.de: Deutsch „ab“ oder „seit“ verleitet zu since. since blickt bis jetzt zurück, hier geht es um einen Stichtag.
wrong.en: German “ab” or “seit” suggests since. since looks back up to now; here it's a key date.

wrong.de: until nennt das Ende einer Dauer. „must go through the new portal“ beginnt aber an diesem Tag.
wrong.en: until names the end of a duration. But “must go through the new portal” starts on that day.

tasks.prompt: Attendance was 1,950, just ___ our target of 2,000.

ok.de: 1,950 liegt knapp unter „2,000“. Etwas knapp darunter heißt just under.
ok.en: 1,950 is slightly below “2,000”. Slightly below is just under.

wrong.de: just over hieße: knapp darüber. 1,950 liegt aber unter „2,000“.
wrong.en: just over would mean slightly above. But 1,950 is below “2,000”.

tasks.prompt: Traffic has doubled, so the new server must handle ___ as many requests as the old one.

ok.de: „has doubled“ heißt: doppelt so viel. Das Vielfache steht direkt vor as many as: twice as many as.
ok.en: “has doubled” means two times as many. The multiple goes right before as many as: twice as many as.

wrong.de: double steht nicht vor as many as. Richtig ist twice as many as.
wrong.en: double doesn't go before as many as. The form is twice as many as.

wrong.de: half as many hieße: halb so viel. „has doubled“ zeigt aber das Doppelte.
wrong.en: half as many would mean half the number. But “has doubled” shows two times as many.

tasks.prompt: Our introductory discount runs ___ Friday, so you still have three days to decide.

ok.de: „runs“ ist ein Zustand, der bis Freitag andauert. Die Dauer bis zu einem Zeitpunkt steht mit until.
ok.en: “runs” is a state that lasts up to Friday. Duration up to a point takes until.

wrong.de: by nennt eine Frist für eine Handlung. „runs“ dauert aber an → until.
wrong.en: by sets a deadline for an action. But “runs” lasts, so use until.

wrong.de: since blickt zurück bis jetzt. „Friday“ liegt hier in der Zukunft.
wrong.en: since looks back up to now. Here “Friday” is in the future.

tasks.prompt: We need the signed NDA ___ Thursday at the latest, before the data room opens.

ok.de: „at the latest“ zeigt eine Frist. Eine Frist für eine einmalige Handlung steht mit by.
ok.en: “at the latest” shows a deadline. A deadline for a one-off action takes by.

wrong.de: Deutsch „bis spätestens“ verleitet zu until. until nennt aber eine Dauer, keine Frist.
wrong.en: German “bis spätestens” suggests until. But until names a duration, not a deadline.

wrong.de: within steht vor einer Zeitspanne (within two days), nicht vor einem Tag wie „Thursday“.
wrong.en: within goes before a time span (within two days), not before a day like “Thursday”.

tasks.prompt: If a delivery arrives damaged, please report it ___ two days.

ok.de: „two days“ ist eine Zeitspanne, an deren Ende spätestens gemeldet wird. Dafür steht within.
ok.en: “two days” is a span by whose end you report at the latest. That takes within.

wrong.de: for nennt, wie lange etwas dauert. Melden ist aber eine einmalige Handlung → within.
wrong.en: for says how long something lasts. But reporting is a one-off action, so use within.

wrong.de: by steht vor einem Zeitpunkt (by Friday). Vor einer Spanne wie „two days“ steht within.
wrong.en: by goes before a point in time (by Friday). Before a span like “two days”, use within.

tasks.prompt: Visitors will need to sign in at the front desk ___ next Monday.

ok.de: „next Monday“ ist der Stichtag, ab dem die Regel gilt. Dafür steht as of.
ok.en: “next Monday” is the key date from which the rule applies. That takes as of.

wrong.de: Deutsch „ab“ verleitet zu since. since blickt aber zurück. „next Monday“ liegt in der Zukunft.
wrong.en: German “ab” suggests since. But since looks back. “next Monday” is in the future.

wrong.de: within steht vor einer Zeitspanne (within a week), nicht vor einem Stichtag wie „next Monday“.
wrong.en: within goes before a time span (within a week), not before a key date like “next Monday”.

tasks.prompt: Thanks to automation, invoice processing now takes a fraction ___ the time it used to.

ok.de: „a fraction“ heißt: ein kleiner Teil davon. Danach folgt hier of: a fraction of.
ok.en: “a fraction” means a small part of something. Here it is followed by of: a fraction of.

wrong.de: Deutsch „ein Bruchteil von“ verleitet zu from. Englisch sagt a fraction of.
wrong.en: German “ein Bruchteil von” suggests from. English says a fraction of.

wrong.de: than gehört zu Vergleichen (cheaper than). Nach „a fraction“ steht of.
wrong.en: than belongs to comparisons (cheaper than). After “a fraction”, use of.

tasks.prompt: The new warehouse is twice as large ___ the old one, so we need more forklifts.

ok.de: „twice as large“ verlangt den Abschluss mit as: twice as large as.
ok.en: “twice as large” must end with as: twice as large as.

wrong.de: Deutsch „größer als“ verleitet zu than. Nach „twice as large“ schließt der Vergleich aber mit as.
wrong.en: German “größer als” suggests than. But after “twice as large”, the comparison closes with as.

wrong.de: Deutsch „so groß wie“ verleitet zu like. Ein Vielfaches mit „twice as large“ schließt aber mit as.
wrong.en: German “so groß wie” suggests like. But a multiple with “twice as large” closes with as.

tasks.prompt: If a customer ___ a refund after 30 days, the system automatically rejects it.

ok.de: „automatically rejects“ beschreibt eine feste Regel. Bei festen Regeln stehen beide Teile im Präsens.
ok.en: “automatically rejects” describes a fixed rule. For fixed rules, both clauses take the present.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht in den if-Satz. Bei einer festen Regel („automatically“) steht dort das Präsens.
wrong.en: will doesn't belong in the if-clause. For a fixed rule (“automatically”), use the present.

wrong.de: a customer ist 3. Person Singular: requests mit -s.
wrong.en: a customer is third-person singular: requests with -s.

tasks.prompt: If the shipment ___ late again, we'll switch to another supplier.

ok.de: „we'll switch“ zeigt eine echte Möglichkeit in der Zukunft. Im if-Satz steht dafür das Präsens.
ok.en: “we'll switch” shows a real future possibility. The if-clause takes the present for it.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn … wird“ verleitet zu will. Im if-Satz steht aber das Präsens: If the shipment arrives.
wrong.en: German “wenn … wird” suggests will. But the if-clause takes the present: If the shipment arrives.

wrong.de: arrived würde eine bloße Annahme machen. Dann müsste es „we'd switch“ heißen, nicht „we'll switch“.
wrong.en: arrived would make it hypothetical. Then the main clause would be “we'd switch”, not “we'll switch”.

tasks.prompt: If the dollar ___ any further, our imports would become far more expensive.

ok.de: „would become“ zeigt eine Annahme. Dann steht im if-Satz das Past Simple: If the dollar fell.
ok.en: “would become” shows a hypothetical. The if-clause then takes the Past Simple: If the dollar fell.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn … fallen würde“ verleitet zu would. would gehört in den Hauptsatz, im if-Satz: fell.
wrong.en: German “wenn … fallen würde” suggests would. would stays in the main clause; the if-clause takes fell.

wrong.de: falls passt zu will im Hauptsatz. Hier steht aber „would become“ → Past Simple: fell.
wrong.en: falls goes with will in the main clause. But here it's “would become”, so use the Past Simple: fell.

tasks.prompt: If I ___ in your position, I'd ask the client to put the commitment in writing.

ok.de: „If I … in your position, I'd“ ist ein Rat als Annahme. Dafür steht were, auch nach I.
ok.en: “If I … in your position, I'd” is advice as a hypothetical. That takes were, even after I.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn ich … wäre“ verleitet zu would be. would gehört in den Hauptsatz („I'd ask“).
wrong.en: German “wenn ich … wäre” suggests would be. would stays in the main clause (“I'd ask”).

wrong.de: am beschreibt eine echte Lage. Du bist aber nicht in seiner Lage → Annahme mit were.
wrong.en: am describes a real situation. But you are not in their position, so use were.

tasks.prompt: If we ___ the contract more carefully, we would have spotted the penalty clause.

ok.de: „would have spotted“ blickt auf eine verpasste Chance. Im if-Satz steht dafür das Past Perfect: had checked.
ok.en: “would have spotted” looks at a missed chance. The if-clause takes the Past Perfect: had checked.

wrong.de: would have gehört in den Hauptsatz. Im if-Satz steht das Past Perfect: If we had checked.
wrong.en: would have belongs in the main clause. The if-clause takes the Past Perfect: If we had checked.

wrong.de: checked allein ist eine Annahme für jetzt. Für die Vergangenheit („would have spotted“) braucht es had checked.
wrong.en: checked alone is a hypothetical about now. For the past (“would have spotted”), use had checked.

tasks.prompt: We'll go ahead with the Friday launch unless QA ___ a serious bug.

ok.de: „unless“ heißt „außer wenn“, die Verneinung steckt schon drin. Danach folgt wie bei if das Präsens.
ok.en: “unless” means “except if”; the negation is built in. Like if, it takes the present.

wrong.de: unless enthält schon das „nicht“. doesn't find würde die Aussage umdrehen.
wrong.en: unless already contains the “not”. doesn't find would reverse the meaning.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht hinter unless. Dort steht das Präsens: unless QA finds.
wrong.en: will doesn't go after unless. Use the present: unless QA finds.

tasks.prompt: When an invoice ___ unpaid for 60 days, it goes to our collections team.

ok.de: „it goes to our collections team“ ist eine feste Regel. Dann stehen beide Teile im Präsens.
ok.en: “it goes to our collections team” is a fixed rule. Then both clauses take the present.

wrong.de: would macht eine Annahme daraus. „it goes“ beschreibt aber eine feste Regel → stays.
wrong.en: would makes it hypothetical. But “it goes” describes a fixed rule, so use stays.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht in den when-Satz. Bei einer Regel („it goes“) steht dort das Präsens.
wrong.en: will doesn't belong in the when-clause. For a rule (“it goes”), use the present.

tasks.prompt: If the client ___ the budget cut, we'll have to drop two features.

ok.de: „we'll have to drop“ zeigt eine echte Möglichkeit. Im if-Satz steht dafür das Präsens: confirms.
ok.en: “we'll have to drop” shows a real possibility. The if-clause takes the present: confirms.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn … wird“ verleitet zu will. will gehört aber in den Hauptsatz („we'll have to“).
wrong.en: German “wenn … wird” suggests will. But will stays in the main clause (“we'll have to”).

wrong.de: confirmed passt zu would im Hauptsatz. Hier steht aber „we'll“ → Präsens: confirms.
wrong.en: confirmed goes with would in the main clause. But here it's “we'll”, so use the present: confirms.

tasks.prompt: If we ___ our prices by 20 percent, we would probably lose half our clients.

ok.de: „would probably lose“ zeigt eine Annahme. Im if-Satz steht dafür das Past Simple: raised.
ok.en: “would probably lose” shows a hypothetical. The if-clause takes the Past Simple: raised.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn wir … erhöhen würden“ verleitet zu would. Im if-Satz steht aber raised.
wrong.en: German “wenn wir … erhöhen würden” suggests would. But the if-clause takes raised.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht in den if-Satz und passt nicht zu „would lose“.
wrong.en: will doesn't belong in the if-clause and doesn't match “would lose”.

tasks.prompt: If it ___ my company, I'd cut the travel budget first.

ok.de: „If it … my company, I'd“ ist eine Annahme: Es ist nicht deine Firma. Dafür steht were.
ok.en: “If it … my company, I'd” is a hypothetical: it isn't your company. That takes were.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn es … wäre“ verleitet zu would be. would gehört in den Hauptsatz („I'd cut“).
wrong.en: German “wenn es … wäre” suggests would be. would stays in the main clause (“I'd cut”).

wrong.de: is beschreibt eine echte Lage und passt nicht zu „I'd cut“. Für eine Annahme: were.
wrong.en: is describes a real situation and doesn't match “I'd cut”. For a hypothetical, use were.

tasks.prompt: We ___ last week's deadline if the supplier had delivered the parts on time.

ok.de: „last week's deadline“ und „had delivered“: eine verpasste Chance. Im Hauptsatz steht would have + Partizip.
ok.en: “last week's deadline” plus “had delivered”: a missed chance. The main clause takes would have + participle.

wrong.de: Deutsch „hätten … geschafft“ verleitet zu had met. Im Hauptsatz steht aber would have met.
wrong.en: German “hätten … geschafft” suggests had met. But the main clause takes would have met.

wrong.de: will meet blickt nach vorn. „last week's deadline“ ist aber schon vorbei.
wrong.en: will meet looks ahead. But “last week's deadline” is already over.

tasks.prompt: I'll present the figures on Monday ___ the auditors approve them by Friday.

ok.de: Du präsentierst unter einer klaren Bedingung („approve them by Friday“). Dafür steht provided that.
ok.en: You present on one condition (“approve them by Friday”). That's provided that.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“. Dann würdest du präsentieren, wenn es keine Freigabe gibt; das ergibt keinen Sinn.
wrong.en: unless means “except if”. You'd present if there were no approval, which makes no sense.

wrong.de: otherwise verbindet keine zwei Satzteile. Es beginnt einen neuen Satz: „… Otherwise, …“
wrong.en: otherwise can't join two clauses. It starts a new sentence: “… Otherwise, …”

tasks.prompt: Unless the bank ___ the loan this month, we'll have to delay the expansion.

ok.de: „Unless“ heißt „wenn … nicht“, die Verneinung steckt schon drin. Danach folgt das Präsens: approves.
ok.en: “Unless” means “if … not”; the negation is built in. The present follows: approves.

wrong.de: unless enthält schon das „nicht“. doesn't approve würde die Aussage umdrehen.
wrong.en: unless already contains the “not”. doesn't approve would reverse the meaning.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht hinter unless. Dort steht das Präsens, will gehört in den Hauptsatz („we'll have to“).
wrong.en: will doesn't go after unless. Use the present there; will stays in the main clause (“we'll have to”).

tasks.prompt: You can work from Lisbon in August as long as you ___ online during core hours.

ok.de: „as long as“ nennt die Bedingung, etwa „nur wenn“. Danach folgt das Präsens, auch wenn es um die Zukunft geht.
ok.en: “as long as” names the condition, like “only if”. The present follows, even for the future.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht hinter „as long as“. Dort steht das Präsens: as long as you stay.
wrong.en: will doesn't go after “as long as”. Use the present: as long as you stay.

wrong.de: stayed macht eine bloße Annahme daraus. „You can work“ ist aber eine echte Möglichkeit → stay.
wrong.en: stayed makes it hypothetical. But “You can work” is a real option, so use stay.

tasks.prompt: Please confirm your seat by Wednesday. ___, we'll offer it to someone on the waiting list.

ok.de: „Please confirm … by Wednesday“: Der zweite Satz nennt die Folge, falls nicht. Am Satzanfang mit Komma: Otherwise.
ok.en: “Please confirm … by Wednesday”: the next sentence gives the result if not. At the start, with a comma: Otherwise.

wrong.de: unless braucht einen Nebensatz (unless you confirm). Als Satzanfang mit Komma passt Otherwise.
wrong.en: unless needs a clause (unless you confirm). At the start of a sentence with a comma, use Otherwise.

tasks.prompt: ___ the quick response of our IT team, we would have lost all the customer data.
accepted: If it had not been for

ok.de: „would have lost“ zeigt: Ohne das hätte es anders geendet. Vor einem Nomen steht dafür But for.
ok.en: “would have lost” shows it would have ended differently without it. Before a noun, use But for.

wrong.de: thanks to nennt den Grund für etwas, das passiert ist. „would have lost“ verlangt aber „ohne“: But for.
wrong.en: thanks to gives the reason for what happened. “would have lost” needs “without”: But for.

wrong.de: unless braucht einen ganzen Satz mit Verb. Vor einem Nomen wie „the quick response“ steht But for.
wrong.en: unless needs a full clause with a verb. Before a noun like “the quick response”, use But for.

tasks.prompt: Had the bank ___ the loan in May, we would have started construction in June.

ok.de: „Had the bank …“ ist ein förmliches if ohne if. Wie beim Past Perfect folgt das Partizip: approved.
ok.en: “Had the bank …” is a formal if without if. As in the Past Perfect, the participle follows: approved.

wrong.de: Nach Had folgt das Partizip, nicht die Grundform: Had the bank approved.
wrong.en: Had is followed by the participle, not the base form: Had the bank approved.

wrong.de: approves passt nicht nach Had. „would have started“ zeigt die Vergangenheit → Had … approved.
wrong.en: approves doesn't follow Had. “would have started” shows the past: Had … approved.

tasks.prompt: I'll print a few extra copies in case more people ___ than we expect.

ok.de: „in case“ nennt eine Vorsorge: Du druckst jetzt, weil es passieren könnte. Danach folgt das Präsens.
ok.en: “in case” names a precaution: you print now because it might happen. The present follows.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht hinter „in case“. Dort steht das Präsens: in case more people show up.
wrong.en: will doesn't go after “in case”. Use the present: in case more people show up.

wrong.de: more people ist Plural: show up ohne -s.
wrong.en: more people is plural: show up without -s.

tasks.prompt: We'll keep our current supplier unless their prices ___ again.

ok.de: „unless“ heißt „wenn … nicht“ und enthält die Verneinung schon. Danach folgt das Präsens: rise.
ok.en: “unless” means “if … not” and already contains the negation. The present follows: rise.

wrong.de: Doppelte Verneinung: unless enthält schon das „nicht“. Mit don't würde die Aussage kippen.
wrong.en: Double negative: unless already contains the “not”. don't would flip the meaning.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht hinter unless. Dort steht das Präsens: unless their prices rise.
wrong.en: will doesn't go after unless. Use the present: unless their prices rise.

tasks.prompt: The client is happy to wait ___ we keep them updated every week.

ok.de: Der Kunde wartet unter einer Bedingung („keep them updated“). Dafür steht as long as.
ok.en: The client waits on one condition (“keep them updated”). That takes as long as.

wrong.de: as far as heißt „soweit“ (as far as I know). Für eine Bedingung steht as long as.
wrong.en: as far as means “to the extent” (as far as I know). For a condition, use as long as.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“. Dann würde der Kunde gerade dann warten, wenn ihr ihn nicht informiert.
wrong.en: unless means “except if”. The client would wait exactly when you didn't update them.

tasks.prompt: We need the final figures by noon. ___, the report can't go out today.

ok.de: Der zweite Satz nennt die Folge, falls die Zahlen fehlen. Für „sonst“ am Satzanfang steht Otherwise.
ok.en: The second sentence gives the result if the figures don't come. For “or else” at the start, use Otherwise.

wrong.de: Unless braucht einen Nebensatz mit Verb (Unless we get …). Allein mit Komma geht es nicht.
wrong.en: Unless needs a clause with a verb (Unless we get …). It can't stand alone with a comma.

wrong.de: In case nennt eine Vorsorge und braucht einen Nebensatz. Für „sonst“ steht Otherwise.
wrong.en: In case names a precaution and needs a clause. For “or else”, use Otherwise.

tasks.prompt: But for ___, we would never have closed the deal in time.

ok.de: Nach „But for“ steht ein Nomen, kein ganzer Satz: But for her quick thinking.
ok.en: “But for” is followed by a noun, not a full clause: But for her quick thinking.

wrong.de: But for kann keinen Satz mit Subjekt und Verb einleiten. Nötig ist ein Nomen: her quick thinking.
wrong.en: But for can't introduce a clause with subject and verb. It needs a noun: her quick thinking.

wrong.de: Auch mit Past Perfect bleibt es ein Satz. Nach But for steht ein Nomen: her quick thinking.
wrong.en: Even with the Past Perfect, it's still a clause. But for takes a noun: her quick thinking.

tasks.prompt: ___ the shipment arrive damaged, please notify us within 48 hours.

ok.de: „please notify us“ ist eine förmliche Bitte für einen möglichen Fall. Bedingung ohne if: Should the shipment arrive …
ok.en: “please notify us” is a formal request for a possible case. A condition without if: Should the shipment arrive …

wrong.de: Would the shipment arrive … wäre eine Frage. Für eine förmliche Bedingung ohne if steht Should.
wrong.en: Would the shipment arrive … would be a question. For a formal condition without if, use Should.

wrong.de: Had braucht ein Partizip und meint die Vergangenheit. Hier geht es um einen möglichen Fall → Should.
wrong.en: Had needs a participle and refers to the past. Here it's a possible future case, so use Should.

tasks.prompt: Take my cell number ___ the hotel loses your reservation.

ok.de: „the hotel loses your reservation“ könnte passieren, du sorgst jetzt vor. Für eine Vorsorge steht in case.
ok.en: “the hotel loses your reservation” might happen, so you act now. A precaution takes in case.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“. Dann sollte man die Nummer gerade dann nehmen, wenn nichts schiefgeht.
wrong.en: unless means “except if”. You'd take the number exactly when nothing went wrong.

wrong.de: otherwise verbindet keine zwei Satzteile. Es beginnt einen neuen Satz.
wrong.en: otherwise can't join two clauses. It starts a new sentence.

tasks.prompt: If we ___ the new planning software last year, our team would work much faster now.

ok.de: „last year“ ist die Ursache in der Vergangenheit, „now“ die Folge heute. Die Ursache steht im Past Perfect: had bought.
ok.en: “last year” is the past cause, “now” the result today. The cause takes the Past Perfect: had bought.

wrong.de: would have gehört nicht in den if-Satz. Für die Ursache „last year“ steht had bought.
wrong.en: would have doesn't belong in the if-clause. For the cause “last year”, use had bought.

wrong.de: bought allein ist eine Annahme für jetzt. „last year“ liegt aber zurück → had bought.
wrong.en: bought alone is a hypothetical about now. But “last year” is in the past, so use had bought.

tasks.prompt: I wish we ___ more developers on the team right now; everyone is overloaded.

ok.de: „right now“ zeigt einen Wunsch für jetzt. Nach wish geht die Form einen Schritt zurück: had.
ok.en: “right now” shows a wish about now. After wish, the form steps back once: had.

wrong.de: wish + would nimmt man für das Verhalten anderer. Für einen Zustand jetzt steht had.
wrong.en: wish + would is for other people's behavior. For a state now, use had.

wrong.de: have beschreibt die Wirklichkeit. Nach wish steht für einen Wunsch jetzt die Vergangenheitsform: had.
wrong.en: After wish, a wish about now takes the past form: had, not have.

tasks.prompt: I wish we ___ the price before we signed the contract.

ok.de: „before we signed“ zeigt: Es geht um Bedauern über die Vergangenheit. Dafür steht wish + Past Perfect.
ok.en: “before we signed” shows regret about the past. That takes wish + Past Perfect.

wrong.de: would have passt nicht nach wish. Für Bedauern über die Vergangenheit steht had negotiated.
wrong.en: would have doesn't follow wish. For regret about the past, use had negotiated.

wrong.de: negotiated allein wäre ein Wunsch für jetzt. „before we signed“ liegt zurück → had negotiated.
wrong.en: negotiated alone would be a wish about now. “before we signed” is past, so use had negotiated.

tasks.prompt: It drives me crazy: I wish our sales reps ___ promising clients features that don't exist.

ok.de: „It drives me crazy“ zeigt: Das Verhalten anderer nervt und soll sich ändern. Dafür steht wish + would.
ok.en: “It drives me crazy” shows others' behavior annoys you and should change. That takes wish + would.

wrong.de: will passt nicht nach wish. Für Ärger über das Verhalten anderer steht would stop.
wrong.en: will doesn't follow wish. For annoyance at others' behavior, use would stop.

wrong.de: stop beschreibt die Wirklichkeit. Nach wish steht für den Wunsch nach Änderung would stop.
wrong.en: stop just describes reality. After wish, a wish for change takes would stop.

tasks.prompt: If our website ___ easier to use, we wouldn't have lost so many customers last year.

ok.de: „easier to use“ ist eine Eigenschaft, die bis heute gilt. Sie erklärt „last year“. Für den Zustand steht were.
ok.en: “easier to use” is a lasting quality that explains “last year”. For that state, use were.

wrong.de: would gehört nicht in den if-Satz. Für die Eigenschaft steht were: If our website were easier.
wrong.en: would doesn't belong in the if-clause. For the quality, use were: If our website were easier.

wrong.de: is beschreibt eine echte Lage. Die Seite ist aber nicht leicht → Annahme mit were.
wrong.en: is describes a real situation. But the site isn't easy to use, so the hypothetical takes were.

tasks.prompt: It's high time we ___ our travel policy; it hasn't changed since 2019.

ok.de: „It's high time“ sagt: Es ist überfällig. Danach steht die Vergangenheitsform, gemeint ist aber jetzt: reviewed.
ok.en: “It's high time” says it's overdue. The past form follows, but the meaning is now: reviewed.

wrong.de: should passt nach „It's high time we“ nicht. Dort steht die Vergangenheitsform: reviewed.
wrong.en: should doesn't follow “It's high time we”. Use the past form: reviewed.

wrong.de: Deutsch „es ist höchste Zeit, dass wir prüfen“ verleitet zum Präsens. Englisch: high time we reviewed.
wrong.en: German “höchste Zeit, dass wir prüfen” suggests the present. English says: high time we reviewed.

tasks.prompt: If we hadn't lost the hotel chain account, we ___ new staff now.

ok.de: „hadn't lost“ ist die Ursache damals, „now“ die Folge heute. Die Folge steht mit would + Grundform.
ok.en: “hadn't lost” is the past cause, “now” the result today. The result takes would + base form.

wrong.de: would have been blickt auf die Vergangenheit. „now“ verlangt die Folge heute → would be hiring.
wrong.en: would have been looks at the past. “now” needs the result today: would be hiring.

wrong.de: will be hiring ist eine echte Zukunft. „hadn't lost“ zeigt aber eine Annahme → would.
wrong.en: will be hiring is a real future. But “hadn't lost” shows a hypothetical, so use would.

tasks.prompt: I wish I ___ more time to prepare, but the pitch is tomorrow morning.

ok.de: „but the pitch is tomorrow“ zeigt einen Wunsch für jetzt. Nach wish geht die Form einen Schritt zurück: had.
ok.en: “but the pitch is tomorrow” shows a wish about now. After wish, the form steps back once: had.

wrong.de: have beschreibt die Wirklichkeit. Nach wish steht für jetzt die Vergangenheitsform: had.
wrong.en: have describes reality. After wish, a wish about now takes the past form: had.

wrong.de: wish + would passt nicht zu dir selbst. Für einen Zustand jetzt steht had.
wrong.en: wish + would isn't used for yourself. For a state now, use had.

tasks.prompt: I wish I ___ that email to the whole team yesterday – it was embarrassing.

ok.de: „yesterday“ und „it was embarrassing“: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit. Dafür steht wish + Past Perfect.
ok.en: “yesterday” plus “it was embarrassing”: regret about the past. That takes wish + Past Perfect.

wrong.de: didn't send wäre ein Wunsch für jetzt. „yesterday“ liegt zurück → zwei Schritte: hadn't sent.
wrong.en: didn't send would be a wish about now. “yesterday” is past, so step back twice: hadn't sent.

wrong.de: wish + would nimmt man für das Verhalten anderer, nicht für eigenes Bedauern.
wrong.en: wish + would is for other people's behavior, not for your own regret.

tasks.prompt: I wish our manager ___ us more notice every time she changes the schedule.

ok.de: „every time“ zeigt: Das Verhalten eines anderen nervt dich. Für diesen Wunsch steht wish + would.
ok.en: “every time” shows someone else's behavior annoys you. That wish takes wish + would.

wrong.de: gives beschreibt die Wirklichkeit. Nach wish steht für den Wunsch nach Änderung would give.
wrong.en: gives just describes reality. After wish, a wish for change takes would give.

wrong.de: will passt nicht nach wish. Für Ärger über andere steht would give.
wrong.en: will doesn't follow wish. For annoyance at others, use would give.

tasks.prompt: If I ___ better with numbers, I would have caught the error in the forecast.

ok.de: „better with numbers“ ist eine Eigenschaft, die bis heute gilt. Sie erklärt den Fehler damals → were.
ok.en: “better with numbers” is a lasting quality that explains the past error, so use were.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wenn ich … wäre“ verleitet zu would be. would gehört in den Hauptsatz.
wrong.en: German “wenn ich … wäre” suggests would be. would stays in the main clause.

wrong.de: am beschreibt eine echte Lage und passt nicht zu „would have caught“. Für die Annahme steht were.
wrong.en: am describes a real situation and doesn't match “would have caught”. The hypothetical takes were.

tasks.prompt: ___ the security update earlier, we wouldn't be dealing with this outage today.

ok.de: „earlier … today“: Förmlich fällt if weg, had rückt vor das Subjekt: Had we installed = If we had installed.
ok.en: “earlier … today”: formally, if is dropped and had moves first: Had we installed = If we had installed.

wrong.de: would have gehört nicht in den if-Satz. Richtig: If we had installed oder förmlich Had we installed.
wrong.en: would have doesn't belong in the if-clause. Correct: If we had installed, or formally Had we installed.

wrong.de: Would we have … ist eine Frage. Für die förmliche Bedingung rückt had nach vorn: Had we installed.
wrong.en: Would we have … is a question. For the formal condition, had moves forward: Had we installed.

tasks.prompt: I was ___ if you could introduce me to your head of procurement.

ok.de: „I was … if you could“: Nach was folgt die -ing-Form. Past + Verlaufsform schafft Abstand, die Bitte ist leicht ablehnbar.
ok.en: “I was … if you could”: was takes the -ing form. Past + progressive adds distance, so the request is easy to decline.

wrong.de: Nach „I was“ fehlt die -ing-Form: I was wondering, nicht I was wonder.
wrong.en: After “I was”, the -ing form is missing: I was wondering, not I was wonder.

wrong.de: was wondered wäre Passiv. Für die höfliche Bitte steht die Verlaufsform: I was wondering.
wrong.en: was wondered would be passive. The polite request takes the progressive: I was wondering.

tasks.prompt: I was wondering whether you ___ the meeting to Thursday afternoon.

ok.de: Nach „I was wondering whether“ bleibt could im Satz, in normaler Wortstellung: whether you could move.
ok.en: After “I was wondering whether”, could stays in the clause, in normal word order: whether you could move.

wrong.de: can passt nicht zu „was wondering“. Die Vergangenheit verlangt could: whether you could move.
wrong.en: can doesn't match “was wondering”. The past form needs could: whether you could move.

wrong.de: will klingt wie eine Frage nach dem Plan. Für eine höfliche Bitte steht could.
wrong.en: will sounds like asking about a plan. For a polite request, use could.

tasks.prompt: We were ___ to finalize the terms before the holidays, if that works for you.

ok.de: „We were … to“: Nach were folgt die -ing-Form. „if that works for you“ zeigt den weichen Wunsch mit Abstand.
ok.en: “We were … to”: were takes the -ing form. “if that works for you” shows a soft wish with distance.

wrong.de: Nach „We were“ fehlt die -ing-Form: We were hoping, nicht We were hope.
wrong.en: After “We were”, the -ing form is missing: We were hoping, not We were hope.

wrong.de: were hoped wäre Passiv. Für den höflichen Wunsch steht die Verlaufsform: We were hoping.
wrong.en: were hoped would be passive. The polite wish takes the progressive: We were hoping.

tasks.prompt: I was hoping you ___ a quick look at the draft before Friday.

ok.de: Nach „I was hoping you“ folgt could, nicht can. So bleibt die Bitte weich und leicht ablehnbar.
ok.en: After “I was hoping you”, could follows, not can. That keeps the request soft and easy to decline.

wrong.de: can passt nicht zu „was hoping“. Die Vergangenheit verlangt could: you could take.
wrong.en: can doesn't match “was hoping”. The past form needs could: you could take.

wrong.de: Nach „hoping you“ folgt kein -ing. Richtig: I was hoping you could take.
wrong.en: “hoping you” isn't followed by -ing. Correct: I was hoping you could take.

tasks.prompt: Would it be possible ___ the invoice in two installments?

ok.de: „Would it be possible“ fragt, ob etwas machbar ist. Danach folgt to + Grundform: to pay.
ok.en: “Would it be possible” asks whether something can be done. To + base form follows: to pay.

wrong.de: Ein that-Satz nach „Would it be possible“ klingt unnatürlich. Üblich ist to + Grundform: to pay.
wrong.en: A that-clause after “Would it be possible” sounds unnatural. Use to + base form: to pay.

wrong.de: Nach possible folgt to + Grundform, nicht -ing: possible to pay.
wrong.en: possible is followed by to + base form, not -ing: possible to pay.

tasks.prompt: Expanding into ten new markets in one year sounds like a bit ___ a stretch.

ok.de: Vor einem Nomen („a stretch“) heißt es a bit of: a bit of a stretch. So klingt der Einwand weich.
ok.en: Before a noun (“a stretch”), it's a bit of: a bit of a stretch. That softens the objection.

wrong.de: a bit too steht vor Adjektiven (a bit too fast). Vor dem Nomen „a stretch“ steht a bit of.
wrong.en: a bit too goes before adjectives (a bit too fast). Before the noun “a stretch”, use a bit of.

tasks.prompt: I was wondering if ___ join us for the client dinner on Thursday.

ok.de: Nach „I was wondering if“ steht normale Wortstellung (you could), keine Frage-Wortstellung.
ok.en: After “I was wondering if”, use normal word order (you could), not question order.

wrong.de: could you ist Frage-Wortstellung. Nach „wondering if“ folgt die normale: you could.
wrong.en: could you is question order. After “wondering if”, normal order follows: you could.

wrong.de: can passt nicht zu „was wondering“. Die Vergangenheit verlangt could.
wrong.en: can doesn't match “was wondering”. The past form needs could.

tasks.prompt: We were hoping ___ a decision from your board by Friday.

ok.de: Nach „were hoping“ folgt to + Grundform: hoping to get.
ok.en: “were hoping” is followed by to + base form: hoping to get.

wrong.de: Nach hoping to folgt die Grundform: to get, nicht to getting.
wrong.en: hoping to is followed by the base form: to get, not to getting.

wrong.de: Nach hoping fehlt hier to: hoping to get.
wrong.en: to is missing after hoping: hoping to get.

tasks.prompt: Would it be possible ___ the kickoff to next Tuesday?

ok.de: „Would it be possible“ fragt nach der Machbarkeit. Danach folgt to + Grundform: to move.
ok.en: “Would it be possible” asks whether something can be done. To + base form follows: to move.

wrong.de: Deutsch „wäre es möglich, dass wir …“ verleitet zum that-Satz. Englisch sagt possible to move.
wrong.en: German “wäre es möglich, dass wir …” suggests a that-clause. English says possible to move.

wrong.de: Nach possible folgt to + Grundform, nicht -ing: possible to move.
wrong.en: possible is followed by to + base form, not -ing: possible to move.

tasks.prompt: Would it be possible ___ to join the call ten minutes early?

ok.de: „Would it be possible … to join“: Die Person steht mit for vor to: possible for you to join.
ok.en: “Would it be possible … to join”: the person goes with for before to: possible for you to join.

wrong.de: that passt nicht vor „to join“. Die Person kommt mit for: possible for you to join.
wrong.en: that can't go before “to join”. The person comes with for: possible for you to join.

wrong.de: Zwischen possible und you fehlt for: possible for you to join.
wrong.en: for is missing between possible and you: possible for you to join.

tasks.prompt: Getting legal sign-off within two weeks may turn out to be ___ headache for us.

ok.de: Vor einem zählbaren Nomen („headache“) steht a bit of a. So wird der Einwand weich.
ok.en: Before a countable noun (“headache”), use a bit of a. That softens the objection.

wrong.de: a bit steht vor Adjektiven (a bit tricky). Vor dem Nomen „headache“ steht a bit of a.
wrong.en: a bit goes before adjectives (a bit tricky). Before the noun “headache”, use a bit of a.

wrong.de: „headache“ ist zählbar und braucht einen Artikel: a bit of a headache.
wrong.en: “headache” is countable and needs an article: a bit of a headache.

tasks.prompt: We'd love to help, but a Monday deadline ___ for us.
options: could be a bit of tricky

ok.de: „We'd love to help, but“ kündigt einen weichen Einwand an. Vor dem Adjektiv tricky steht a bit, nach could be.
ok.en: “We'd love to help, but” signals a soft objection. Before the adjective tricky, use a bit, after could be.

wrong.opt: could be a bit of tricky
wrong.de: a bit of steht vor Nomen (a bit of a stretch). Vor dem Adjektiv tricky steht a bit allein.
wrong.en: a bit of goes before nouns (a bit of a stretch). Before the adjective tricky, use just a bit.

wrong.de: Nach could folgt die Grundform: could be, nicht could being.
wrong.en: could is followed by the base form: could be, not could being.

tasks.prompt: Our security logs ___ every Monday morning by the IT team.

ok.de: „every Monday morning“ ist eine Routine, und die Logs prüfen nicht selbst: Passiv Simple, are + 3. Form.
ok.en: “every Monday morning” is a routine, and the logs don't review anything: simple passive, are + past participle.

wrong.de: „become reviewed“ kommt vom deutschen „werden“. become heißt „sich verändern“. Das Passiv braucht be: are reviewed.
wrong.en: “become reviewed” comes from German “werden”. become means “change into”. The passive needs be: are reviewed.

wrong.de: „are reviewing“ ist aktiv: Die Logs würden selbst prüfen. Hier werden sie geprüft: are reviewed.
wrong.en: “are reviewing” is active: the logs would do the reviewing. Here they are reviewed.

tasks.prompt: Your refund ___ to your card three days ago, so it should appear soon.

ok.de: „three days ago“ nennt einen fertigen Zeitpunkt, und die Erstattung wird geschickt: Passiv im Past Simple, was sent.
ok.en: “three days ago” names a finished time, and the refund is sent by someone: simple passive in the past, was sent.

wrong.de: „has been sent“ passt nicht zu „three days ago“. Ein fertiger Zeitpunkt verlangt das Past Simple: was sent.
wrong.en: “has been sent” doesn't fit “three days ago”. A finished time needs the past simple: was sent.

wrong.de: send ist unregelmäßig: send – sent – sent. Also was sent.
wrong.en: send is irregular: send – sent – sent. So: was sent.

tasks.prompt: Sorry, the projector in Room 4 ___ at the moment, so let's use Room 6.

ok.de: „at the moment“ zeigt: Es passiert gerade mit dem Beamer. Dafür braucht das Passiv being: is being repaired.
ok.en: “at the moment” shows it is happening to the projector now. The passive needs being: is being repaired.

wrong.de: „is repaired“ heißt „ist (fertig) repariert“ oder „wird regelmäßig repariert“. Für „at the moment“ fehlt being.
wrong.en: “is repaired” means “is fixed” or “is repaired regularly”. For “at the moment” you need being.

wrong.de: „is repairing“ ist aktiv: Der Beamer würde selbst reparieren. Er wird repariert: is being repaired.
wrong.en: “is repairing” is active: the projector would be doing the repairs. It is being repaired.

tasks.prompt: This training manual ___ since 2019, so some of the steps may be outdated.

ok.de: „since 2019“ reicht bis heute: Present Perfect. Das Handbuch wird nicht aktualisiert: hasn't been updated.
ok.en: “since 2019” runs up to now: present perfect. The manual isn't updated by itself: hasn't been updated.

wrong.de: „isn't updated since“ ist die deutsche Falle („wird seit 2019 nicht aktualisiert“). Mit since steht Present Perfect.
wrong.en: “isn't updated since” copies German present with “seit”. With since, English uses the present perfect.

wrong.de: „wasn't updated“ endet in der Vergangenheit. „since 2019“ reicht bis jetzt: hasn't been updated.
wrong.en: “wasn't updated” ends in the past. “since 2019” reaches up to now: hasn't been updated.

tasks.prompt: I can confirm that the signed contracts ___ to you by courier before the end of next week.

ok.de: „before the end of next week“ liegt in der Zukunft, und die Verträge werden geliefert: will be + 3. Form.
ok.en: “before the end of next week” is in the future, and the contracts are delivered by someone: will be + participle.

wrong.de: „will deliver“ ist aktiv: Die Verträge würden selbst liefern. Passiv braucht will be delivered.
wrong.en: “will deliver” is active: the contracts would do the delivering. The passive needs will be delivered.

wrong.de: „are delivered“ klingt nach Routine. Für „before the end of next week“ braucht es die Zukunft: will be delivered.
wrong.en: “are delivered” sounds like a routine. “before the end of next week” needs the future: will be delivered.

tasks.prompt: The safety inspection at our plant ___ by an outside firm last Thursday.

ok.de: „last Thursday“ ist abgeschlossen: was + 3. Form. Die Partikel bleibt beim Verb: was carried out, dann by.
ok.en: “last Thursday” is finished: was + participle. The particle stays with the verb: was carried out, then by.

wrong.de: „has been carried out“ passt nicht zu „last Thursday“. Fertiger Zeitpunkt heißt Past Simple: was carried out.
wrong.en: “has been carried out” doesn't fit “last Thursday”. A finished time needs the past simple: was carried out.

wrong.de: Ohne out ändert sich die Bedeutung: „was carried“ heißt „wurde getragen“. Es heißt was carried out.
wrong.en: Without out the meaning changes: “was carried” means it was physically carried. Say was carried out.

tasks.prompt: Most of our spare parts ___ in a small plant near Detroit.

ok.de: Die Teile werden hergestellt, sie stellen nichts her. Allgemeine Tatsache „in a small plant“: are produced.
ok.en: The parts are made; they don't make anything. A general fact about “a small plant”: are produced.

wrong.de: „become“ kommt vom deutschen „werden“, heißt aber „sich verändern“. Das Passiv bildet man mit be: are produced.
wrong.en: “become” comes from German “werden” but means “change into”. The passive uses be: are produced.

wrong.de: „are producing“ ist aktiv: Die Teile würden selbst etwas herstellen. Sie werden hergestellt: are produced.
wrong.en: “are producing” is active: the parts would be making something. They are made: are produced.

tasks.prompt: Please don't use the shared drive – the files ___ to the new server at the moment.

ok.de: „at the moment“ zeigt: Es passiert jetzt mit den Dateien. Passiv mit being: are being copied.
ok.en: “at the moment” shows it is happening to the files now. Passive with being: are being copied.

wrong.de: „are copied“ beschreibt eine Routine. Für „at the moment“ braucht das Passiv being: are being copied.
wrong.en: “are copied” describes a routine. For “at the moment” the passive needs being: are being copied.

wrong.de: „are copying“ ist aktiv: Die Dateien würden selbst kopieren. Sie werden kopiert: are being copied.
wrong.en: “are copying” is active: the files would be copying something. They are being copied.

tasks.prompt: So far, only three of the twelve invoices ___ by the client.

ok.de: „So far“ heißt „bis jetzt“: Present Perfect. Die Rechnungen werden bezahlt: have been paid.
ok.en: “So far” means “up to now”: present perfect. The invoices are paid by someone: have been paid.

wrong.de: „were paid“ schließt ab. „So far“ reicht bis jetzt, deshalb Present Perfect: have been paid.
wrong.en: “were paid” closes the matter. “So far” reaches up to now, so present perfect: have been paid.

wrong.de: „are paid“ klingt nach Routine. „So far“ zählt bis heute: have been paid.
wrong.en: “are paid” sounds like a routine. “So far” counts up to today: have been paid.

tasks.prompt: Visitor badges ___ at reception before you leave the building.

ok.de: „Visitor badges“ geben nichts zurück, sie werden zurückgegeben. Nach must steht be + 3. Form: must be returned.
ok.en: “Visitor badges” don't return anything; they are returned. After must comes be + participle: must be returned.

wrong.de: „must return“ ist aktiv: Die Ausweise würden selbst etwas zurückgeben. Passiv: must be returned.
wrong.en: “must return” is active: the badges would do the returning. Passive: must be returned.

wrong.de: Nach must fehlt be. Das Modalpassiv ist must + be + 3. Form: must be returned.
wrong.en: be is missing after must. The modal passive is must + be + participle: must be returned.

tasks.prompt: The new travel policy was approved ___ the finance committee on Tuesday.

ok.de: Der Handelnde im Passiv („the finance committee“) steht nach by: was approved by.
ok.en: In the passive, the agent (“the finance committee”) comes after by: was approved by.

wrong.de: „from“ kommt vom deutschen „von“. Den Handelnden im Passiv leitet by ein.
wrong.en: “from” copies German “von”. In the passive, the agent is introduced with by.

wrong.de: „approved of“ heißt „gutheißen“ und passt nicht zum Handelnden „the finance committee“. Es heißt approved by.
wrong.en: “approved of” means “liked the idea” and doesn't introduce the agent. Say approved by.

tasks.prompt: The billing error ___ by the IT team, and they'll call you later today.

ok.de: Der Fehler wird geprüft („by the IT team“). Passiv: has been looked into, die Präposition into bleibt beim Verb.
ok.en: The error is checked “by the IT team”. Passive: has been looked into, and into stays with the verb.

wrong.de: „has looked into“ ist aktiv: Der Fehler würde selbst prüfen. Mit „by the IT team“ braucht es been.
wrong.en: “has looked into” is active: the error would do the checking. With “by the IT team” you need been.

wrong.de: Ohne into fehlt die feste Präposition: look into heißt „prüfen“. Sie bleibt im Passiv stehen.
wrong.en: Without into the fixed preposition is missing: look into means “check”. It stays in the passive.

tasks.prompt: All travel requests need to ___ by your team lead before you book anything.

ok.de: Nach „need to“ kommt im Passiv be + 3. Form: Die Anträge werden genehmigt, also be approved.
ok.en: After “need to”, the passive is be + participle: the requests are approved by someone, so be approved.

wrong.de: Nach „need to“ steht die Grundform be, nicht been: need to be approved.
wrong.en: After “need to” you need the base form be, not been: need to be approved.

wrong.de: Es fehlt be. Deutsch stellt „werden“ ans Ende („genehmigt werden“), Englisch braucht be direkt nach „need to“.
wrong.en: be is missing. German puts “werden” at the end; English needs be right after “need to”.

wrong.de: „need to approve“ ist aktiv: Die Anträge würden selbst genehmigen. Sie werden genehmigt: be approved.
wrong.en: “need to approve” is active: the requests would do the approving. They are approved: be approved.

tasks.prompt: By the time our team arrived at the client's office, the main decision ___.

ok.de: „By the time our team arrived“ zeigt: Es war schon vorher passiert. Davor-Vergangenheit im Passiv: had been made.
ok.en: “By the time our team arrived” shows it happened earlier. Past perfect passive: had been made.

wrong.de: „was made“ klingt, als passierte es erst bei der Ankunft. „By the time“ verlangt had been made.
wrong.en: “was made” sounds as if it happened when we arrived. “By the time” needs had been made.

wrong.de: „has been made“ passt nicht zur Vergangenheit „arrived“. Vor einem Punkt in der Vergangenheit: had been made.
wrong.en: “has been made” doesn't fit the past “arrived”. Before a past moment use had been made.

tasks.prompt: Three of our five warehouses ___ since the start of the year.

ok.de: „since the start of the year“ reicht bis heute: Present Perfect. Die Lager werden verkauft: have been sold.
ok.en: “since the start of the year” runs up to now: present perfect. The warehouses are sold: have been sold.

wrong.de: „were sold“ schließt ab. Mit „since“ reicht der Zeitraum bis jetzt: have been sold.
wrong.en: “were sold” closes the period. With “since” it runs up to now: have been sold.

wrong.de: „are sold since“ folgt dem Deutschen („seit … verkauft“). Mit since steht Present Perfect: have been sold.
wrong.en: “are sold since” copies German. With since, English uses the present perfect: have been sold.

tasks.prompt: The new CFO ___ to be quite tough on travel costs.

ok.de: Man gibt wieder, was andere sagen („to be quite tough“): X is said to … Deutsch: „Er soll recht hart sein.“
ok.en: You report what people say (“to be quite tough”): X is said to … This is the neutral reporting form.

wrong.de: „says to be“ hieße, der CFO sagt etwas. Gemeint ist: Andere sagen es über ihn, also is said to be.
wrong.en: “says to be” would mean the CFO says something. Others say it about him: is said to be.

wrong.de: „should“ übersetzt das deutsche „soll“, heißt aber „sollte“. Für Gerüchte nimmt man is said to.
wrong.en: “should” copies German “soll” but means advice. For reports and rumors use is said to.

tasks.prompt: Our main competitor is reported ___ about 200 jobs last quarter.

ok.de: „last quarter“ liegt vor dem Bericht. Für Vergangenes nach is reported steht to have + 3. Form: to have cut.
ok.en: “last quarter” is before the report. For an earlier action after is reported, use to have + participle.

wrong.de: „to cut“ meint jetzt oder später. Wegen „last quarter“ braucht es to have cut.
wrong.en: “to cut” refers to now or later. Because of “last quarter” you need to have cut.

wrong.de: Nach is reported steht to + Grundform, kein -ing. Für die Vergangenheit: to have cut.
wrong.en: After is reported comes to + base form, not -ing. For the past: to have cut.

tasks.prompt: Our new hires really appreciate ___ to client calls from day one.

ok.de: Nach „appreciate“ steht -ing. Die Neuen werden eingeladen, also Passiv mit -ing: being invited.
ok.en: After “appreciate” comes -ing. The new hires are invited, so the -ing passive: being invited.

wrong.de: „to be invited“ folgt dem Deutschen („eingeladen zu werden“). Nach appreciate steht -ing: being invited.
wrong.en: “to be invited” copies German “eingeladen zu werden”. After appreciate use -ing: being invited.

wrong.de: „inviting“ ist aktiv: Die Neuen würden einladen. Sie werden eingeladen: being invited.
wrong.en: “inviting” is active: the new hires would do the inviting. They are invited: being invited.

tasks.prompt: The final slides ___ checked by legal before we send them to the client.

ok.de: Die Folien werden geprüft („by legal“). Nach have to kommt be + 3. Form: have to be checked.
ok.en: The slides are checked “by legal”. After have to comes be + participle: have to be checked.

wrong.de: Es fehlt be. „have to checked“ ist kein Satz. Im Passiv: have to be checked.
wrong.en: be is missing. “have to checked” is not English. The passive needs have to be checked.

wrong.de: Nach to steht die Grundform be, nicht been: have to be checked.
wrong.en: After to you need the base form be, not been: have to be checked.

tasks.prompt: Sorry, this order ___ before Monday because the warehouse is closed this weekend.

ok.de: Die Bestellung bearbeitet nichts, sie wird bearbeitet („the warehouse is closed“). Nach can't: be + 3. Form.
ok.en: The order doesn't process anything; it is processed (“the warehouse is closed”). After can't: be + participle.

wrong.de: „can't process“ ist aktiv: Die Bestellung würde selbst bearbeiten. Passiv: can't be processed.
wrong.en: “can't process” is active: the order would be doing the processing. Passive: can't be processed.

wrong.de: Nach can't fehlt be. Das Modalpassiv ist can't + be + 3. Form.
wrong.en: be is missing after can't. The modal passive is can't + be + participle.

tasks.prompt: The replacement part ___ last Friday, but the client says it never arrived.

ok.de: „last Friday“ ist ein fertiger Zeitpunkt: Past Simple im Passiv, was delivered.
ok.en: “last Friday” is a finished time: past simple passive, was delivered.

wrong.de: Deutsch sagt „ist letzten Freitag geliefert worden“. Englisch verbietet Present Perfect mit „last Friday“.
wrong.en: German allows the perfect with “last Friday”. English doesn't: a finished time needs was delivered.

wrong.de: „had delivered“ ist aktiv: Das Teil würde selbst liefern. Es wird geliefert: was delivered.
wrong.en: “had delivered” is active: the part would do the delivering. It was delivered.

tasks.prompt: The two banks ___ to be in talks about a possible merger.

ok.de: Man gibt eine Vermutung anderer wieder („to be in talks“): X is/are believed to … = „Man glaubt, dass …“.
ok.en: You report what others think (“to be in talks”): X are believed to … = people believe that …

wrong.de: „The two banks believe to be“ hieße, die Banken glauben etwas. Andere glauben es: are believed to be.
wrong.en: “The two banks believe to be” would mean the banks believe something. Others do: are believed to be.

wrong.de: believe steht nicht in der -ing-Form, und es ist aktiv. Für die Vermutung anderer: are believed to.
wrong.en: believe isn't used in the -ing form here, and it's active. For what others think: are believed to.

tasks.prompt: She left the office early to avoid ___ into another long meeting.

ok.de: Nach „avoid“ steht -ing. Sie wird hineingezogen, also Passiv mit -ing: being pulled.
ok.en: After “avoid” comes -ing. She is pulled in by others, so the -ing passive: being pulled.

wrong.de: Nach avoid steht -ing, kein to: „avoid to be“ ist falsch. Richtig: avoid being pulled.
wrong.en: avoid takes -ing, not to: “avoid to be” is wrong. Say avoid being pulled.

wrong.de: „avoid pulling“ ist aktiv: Sie würde jemanden hineinziehen. Gemeint ist, dass sie gezogen wird.
wrong.en: “avoid pulling” is active: she would pull someone in. The idea is that she is pulled in.

tasks.prompt: The intern was added to the project without ___ by anyone.

ok.de: Nach „without“ steht -ing. „by anyone“ zeigt: Niemand fragte ihn. Passiv mit -ing: being asked.
ok.en: After “without” comes -ing. “by anyone” shows nobody asked him. The -ing passive: being asked.

wrong.de: „without asking“ ist aktiv: Er hätte nicht gefragt. „by anyone“ verlangt Passiv: being asked.
wrong.en: “without asking” is active: he didn't ask. “by anyone” needs the passive: being asked.

wrong.de: Nach without steht kein to. Das deutsche „ohne gefragt zu werden“ wird zu without being asked.
wrong.en: without takes -ing, not to. German “ohne gefragt zu werden” becomes without being asked.

tasks.prompt: Last spring, the vendor said the update ___ ready by June, but it came in August.

ok.de: „Last spring … said“ liegt zurück, und die Aussage ist überholt („came in August“): will rückt zu would.
ok.en: “Last spring … said” is in the past, and the claim is outdated (“came in August”): will shifts to would.

wrong.de: „will be“ bleibt in der Gegenwart stehen. Die Aussage ist vorbei („came in August“): would be.
wrong.en: “will be” stays in the present. The statement is over (“came in August”): would be.

wrong.de: „is“ passt nicht: Juni ist vorbei, und es geht um eine Zusage für später. will wird would: would be.
wrong.en: “is” doesn't fit: June is over, and this was a promise about later. will becomes would: would be.

tasks.prompt: Back in March, Omar wrote that the shipment had left the port ___.

ok.de: Omar schrieb das „Back in March“. Sein „yesterday“ zählt von damals aus: the day before.
ok.en: Omar wrote this “Back in March”. His “yesterday” counts from then: the day before.

wrong.de: „yesterday“ hieße „gestern von heute aus“. Gemeint ist der Tag vor seiner Mail im März: the day before.
wrong.en: “yesterday” would mean the day before today. He means the day before his email in March: the day before.

wrong.de: „the last day“ heißt „der letzte Tag“. Für „gestern“ in indirekter Rede: the day before.
wrong.en: “the last day” means the final day. For “yesterday” in reported speech say the day before.

tasks.prompt: During her visit last week, the auditor asked us ___ the old contracts.

ok.de: „asked us“ leitet eine indirekte Frage ein: Fragewort + Subjekt + Verb, ohne did: where we kept.
ok.en: “asked us” introduces a reported question: question word + subject + verb, no did: where we kept.

wrong.de: „where did we keep“ ist die direkte Frage. Nach „asked us“ fällt did weg: where we kept.
wrong.en: “where did we keep” is the direct question. After “asked us” drop did: where we kept.

wrong.de: Das Verb steht nach dem Subjekt, wie im Aussagesatz: where we kept.
wrong.en: The verb comes after the subject, as in a statement: where we kept.

tasks.prompt: Our team lead ___ us that the review had moved to Thursday.

ok.de: Direkt danach steht eine Person („us“). Mit Person nimmt man tell: told us.
ok.en: A person (“us”) follows directly. With a person you use tell: told us.

wrong.de: „said us“ folgt dem deutschen „sagte uns“. say steht ohne Person. Mit „us“: told us.
wrong.en: “said us” copies German “sagte uns”. say takes no person. With “us”: told us.

wrong.de: „had moved“ zeigt: Es ist Vergangenheit. Also told.
wrong.en: “had moved” shows this is in the past. So: told.

tasks.prompt: The client asked us ___ the logo until after their board meeting.

ok.de: Eine Bitte nach „asked us“ wird zu not to + Grundform: not to change.
ok.en: A request after “asked us” becomes not to + base form: not to change.

wrong.de: „don't change“ übernimmt die direkte Bitte. Indirekt heißt es asked us not to change.
wrong.en: “don't change” keeps the direct request. Reported, it is asked us not to change.

wrong.de: Nach „asked us“ steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: not to change.
wrong.en: After “asked us” comes to + base form, not -ing: not to change.

tasks.prompt: Security told all visitors ___ their badges at the front desk.

ok.de: Eine Anweisung nach „told all visitors“ wird zu to + Grundform: to leave.
ok.en: An instruction after “told all visitors” becomes to + base form: to leave.

wrong.de: Nach told + Person steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: told them to leave.
wrong.en: After told + person comes to + base form, not -ing: told them to leave.

wrong.de: „told all visitors should leave“ fehlt that/they. Kurz und richtig: told all visitors to leave.
wrong.en: “told all visitors should leave” lacks a subject. Short and correct: told all visitors to leave.

tasks.prompt: Last October, the supplier promised that prices ___ stable for a year, but they rose in May.

ok.de: „Last October … promised“ ist vorbei, und die Zusage ist überholt („rose in May“): will rückt zu would.
ok.en: “Last October … promised” is over, and the promise is outdated (“rose in May”): will shifts to would.

wrong.de: „will stay“ bleibt in der Gegenwart. Die Zusage ist überholt („rose in May“), also would stay.
wrong.en: “will stay” stays in the present. The promise is outdated (“rose in May”), so would stay.

wrong.de: „stay“ klingt nach heute. Die Preise sind gestiegen („rose in May“), die Zusage ist alt: would stay.
wrong.en: “stay” sounds like today. Prices “rose in May”, so the promise is old: would stay.

tasks.prompt: Back in May, Priya told me she was swamped ___, so we postponed our call.

ok.de: Priya sagte das „Back in May“. Ihr „this week“ meint eine Woche im Mai: that week.
ok.en: Priya said this “Back in May”. Her “this week” means a week in May: that week.

wrong.de: „this week“ hieße die Woche von heute. Gemeint ist die Woche im Mai: that week.
wrong.en: “this week” would mean the current week. She means a week in May: that week.

wrong.de: „was swamped next week“ passt nicht: „was“ beschreibt die Lage damals, nicht später.
wrong.en: “was swamped next week” doesn't work: “was” describes the situation then, not later.

tasks.prompt: During yesterday's kickoff call, the new client asked me ___.
tasks.answer: how long the project would take
options: how long the project would take
how long would the project take
how long will take the project

ok.de: Nach „asked me“ folgt die Satzstellung des Aussagesatzes: Subjekt vor Verb, the project would take.
ok.en: After “asked me” use statement order: subject before verb, the project would take.

wrong.opt: how long would the project take
wrong.de: Das ist die Stellung der direkten Frage. Nach „asked me“ steht das Subjekt vorn: the project would take.
wrong.en: That is direct question order. After “asked me” the subject comes first: the project would take.

wrong.opt: how long will take the project
wrong.de: Das Subjekt fehlt vor dem Verb, und will rückt nach „asked“ zu would: the project would take.
wrong.en: The subject must come before the verb, and will shifts to would after “asked”.

tasks.prompt: Finance wanted to know ___ the receipts with the expense report.

ok.de: „wanted to know“ leitet eine Ja/Nein-Frage ein: if + Subjekt + Verb, also if we had sent.
ok.en: “wanted to know” introduces a yes/no question: if + subject + verb, so if we had sent.

wrong.de: Das ist die Stellung der direkten Frage. Indirekt: if + Subjekt + Verb, if we had sent.
wrong.en: That is direct question order. Reported: if + subject + verb, if we had sent.

wrong.de: „that“ leitet eine Aussage ein. „wanted to know“ ist eine Frage: if oder whether.
wrong.en: “that” introduces a statement. “wanted to know” is a question: use if or whether.

tasks.prompt: At the all-hands meeting, she ___ to everyone that the launch was on track.

ok.de: „to everyone“ steht mit to. Das geht mit say: said to everyone. tell nimmt die Person ohne to.
ok.en: “to everyone” comes with to. That works with say: said to everyone. tell takes the person without to.

wrong.de: tell steht ohne to: told everyone. Mit „to everyone“ passt said.
wrong.en: tell takes no to: told everyone. With “to everyone”, said fits.

wrong.de: „told to“ ergäbe „told to to everyone“. tell steht ohne to; mit „to everyone“ passt said.
wrong.en: “told to” would give “told to to everyone”. tell takes no to; with “to everyone”, said fits.

tasks.prompt: Before the update last night, IT asked everyone ___ their laptops switched on.

ok.de: Eine Bitte nach „asked everyone“ wird zu to + Grundform: to leave.
ok.en: A request after “asked everyone” becomes to + base form: to leave.

wrong.de: Nach asked + Person steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: asked everyone to leave.
wrong.en: After asked + person comes to + base form, not -ing: asked everyone to leave.

wrong.de: „asked everyone they leave“ ist kein Satz. Die Bitte wird zu to + Grundform: to leave.
wrong.en: “asked everyone they leave” isn't English. The request becomes to + base form: to leave.

tasks.prompt: The contractor finally admitted ___ the wrong cables in the server room.

ok.de: Nach „admitted“ steht die -ing-Form: admitted installing. Deutsch sagt „zugeben, … zu haben“.
ok.en: After “admitted” comes the -ing form: admitted installing.

wrong.de: „admitted to install“ folgt dem deutschen „zu installieren“. Nach admit steht -ing: admitted installing.
wrong.en: “admitted to install” copies German “zu installieren”. After admit use -ing: admitted installing.

wrong.de: Direkt nach „admitted“ steht hier die -ing-Form, nicht die Vergangenheit: admitted installing.
wrong.en: Right after “admitted” use the -ing form, not the past: admitted installing.

tasks.prompt: Our consultant suggested ___ the kickoff until the new budget is approved.

ok.de: Nach „suggested“ steht -ing (oder ein that-Satz): suggested delaying.
ok.en: After “suggested” comes -ing (or a that-clause): suggested delaying.

wrong.de: „suggested to delay“ folgt dem deutschen „vorschlagen, zu verschieben“. Nach suggest: -ing.
wrong.en: “suggested to delay” copies German “vorschlagen, zu verschieben”. After suggest use -ing.

wrong.de: „suggested us to“ gibt es nicht. Richtig: suggested delaying oder suggested that we delay.
wrong.en: “suggested us to” is not English. Say suggested delaying or suggested that we delay.

tasks.prompt: The new client insisted ___ every contract in person at our office.

ok.de: „insisted“ braucht on + -ing: insisted on signing. Das „darauf“ im Deutschen ist hier das on.
ok.en: “insisted” needs on + -ing: insisted on signing.

wrong.de: „insisted to sign“ folgt „bestand darauf, zu unterschreiben“. Englisch: insisted on signing.
wrong.en: “insisted to sign” copies German “darauf bestehen, zu …”. English: insisted on signing.

wrong.de: Es fehlt on. Nach insist steht on + -ing: insisted on signing.
wrong.en: on is missing. insist takes on + -ing: insisted on signing.

tasks.prompt: The bank warned us ___ the transfer until the account details were confirmed.

ok.de: Nach „warned us“ folgt not to + Grundform: warned us not to make.
ok.en: After “warned us” comes not to + base form: warned us not to make.

wrong.de: Nach warn + Person steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: warned us not to make.
wrong.en: After warn + person comes to + base form, not -ing: warned us not to make.

wrong.de: „don't make“ übernimmt die direkte Warnung. Indirekt: warned us not to make.
wrong.en: “don't make” keeps the direct warning. Reported: warned us not to make.

tasks.prompt: Our new supplier offered ___ the setup fee if we sign the contract this month.

ok.de: Nach „offered“ steht to + Grundform: offered to waive.
ok.en: After “offered” comes to + base form: offered to waive.

wrong.de: „offered waiving“ überträgt die -ing-Regel von suggest. Nach offer steht to: offered to waive.
wrong.en: “offered waiving” copies the -ing rule from suggest. offer takes to: offered to waive.

tasks.prompt: After a long discussion, the supplier agreed ___ its prices by five percent.

ok.de: Nach „agreed“ steht to + Grundform: agreed to cut.
ok.en: After “agreed” comes to + base form: agreed to cut.

wrong.de: Nach agree steht kein -ing. Richtig: agreed to cut.
wrong.en: agree isn't followed by -ing. Say agreed to cut.

wrong.de: „agreed on“ steht vor einem Nomen („agreed on a price“). Mit Verb: agreed to cut.
wrong.en: “agreed on” goes before a noun (“agreed on a price”). With a verb: agreed to cut.

tasks.prompt: The project manager firmly denied ___ the draft budget to the press.

ok.de: Nach „denied“ steht die -ing-Form: denied leaking.
ok.en: After “denied” comes the -ing form: denied leaking.

wrong.de: „denied to leak“ folgt dem deutschen „bestreiten, … zu haben“. Nach deny: -ing.
wrong.en: “denied to leak” copies German “bestreiten, zu …”. After deny use -ing.

wrong.de: Auch für Vergangenes steht nach deny kein to. Möglich: denied leaking oder denied having leaked.
wrong.en: Even for the past, deny takes no to. Say denied leaking or denied having leaked.

tasks.prompt: Finance recommended ___ the old laptops instead of buying new ones this year.

ok.de: Nach „recommended“ steht -ing (oder ein that-Satz): recommended repairing.
ok.en: After “recommended” comes -ing (or a that-clause): recommended repairing.

wrong.de: Zwei Verben stoßen ohne Verbindung aufeinander. Nach recommend: -ing oder that we repair.
wrong.en: Two verbs can't just sit side by side. After recommend use -ing or that we repair.

wrong.de: „recommended to repair“ folgt „empfehlen, zu reparieren“. Nach recommend: -ing.
wrong.en: “recommended to repair” copies German “empfehlen, zu …”. After recommend use -ing.

tasks.prompt: Our CEO insisted ___ the final decision on the new office herself.

ok.de: „insisted“ braucht on + -ing: insisted on making.
ok.en: “insisted” needs on + -ing: insisted on making.

wrong.de: „insisted to make“ folgt „bestand darauf, zu treffen“. Englisch: insisted on making.
wrong.en: “insisted to make” copies German “darauf bestehen, zu …”. English: insisted on making.

wrong.de: Es fehlt on. Nach insist steht on + -ing: insisted on making.
wrong.en: on is missing. insist takes on + -ing: insisted on making.

tasks.prompt: The consultant advised ___ the fine print carefully before signing anything.

ok.de: „advised“ + to-Verb braucht die Person direkt danach: advised us to check.
ok.en: “advised” + to-verb needs the person right after it: advised us to check.

wrong.de: Deutsch sagt „riet, … zu prüfen“ ohne Person. Englisch braucht sie: advised us to check.
wrong.en: German can drop the person. English needs it before to: advised us to check.

wrong.de: Nach advise + Person steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: advised us to check.
wrong.en: After advise + person comes to + base form, not -ing: advised us to check.

tasks.prompt: Our travel agent warned us ___ money at the airport because of the high fees.

ok.de: Nach „warned us“ folgt not to + Grundform: warned us not to exchange.
ok.en: After “warned us” comes not to + base form: warned us not to exchange.

wrong.de: Nach warn + Person steht to + Grundform, kein -ing: not to exchange.
wrong.en: After warn + person comes to + base form, not -ing: not to exchange.

wrong.de: „don't exchange“ übernimmt die direkte Warnung. Indirekt: warned us not to exchange.
wrong.en: “don't exchange” keeps the direct warning. Reported: warned us not to exchange.

tasks.prompt: My colleague promised ___ me the slides before the client meeting.

ok.de: Nach „promised“ steht to + Grundform: promised to send.
ok.en: After “promised” comes to + base form: promised to send.

wrong.de: „promised sending“ überträgt die -ing-Regel von suggest. Nach promise: to send.
wrong.en: “promised sending” copies the -ing rule from suggest. promise takes to: to send.

wrong.de: Nach promise fehlt to: promised to send.
wrong.en: to is missing after promise: promised to send.

tasks.prompt: Could you tell me how long ___ to process a refund at your company?

ok.de: „Could you tell me“ macht die Frage indirekt: Subjekt + Verb wie im Aussagesatz, ohne does: it usually takes.
ok.en: “Could you tell me” makes it indirect: subject + verb as in a statement, no does: it usually takes.

wrong.de: „does it usually take“ ist die direkte Frage. Nach „Could you tell me“ fällt does weg: it usually takes.
wrong.en: “does it usually take” is the direct question. After “Could you tell me” drop does: it usually takes.

wrong.de: Ohne does trägt das Verb selbst das -s: it usually takes.
wrong.en: Without does, the verb itself takes the -s: it usually takes.

tasks.prompt: The client wants to know ___ the price includes installation and training.

ok.de: „wants to know“ leitet eine Ja/Nein-Frage ein (Ist es enthalten?). Dafür steht if oder whether.
ok.en: “wants to know” introduces a yes/no question (Is it included?). Use if or whether.

wrong.de: „that“ leitet eine Aussage ein. Der Kunde fragt aber etwas: if oder whether.
wrong.en: “that” introduces a statement. The client is asking something: use if or whether.

wrong.de: „does“ gehört in die direkte Frage. Indirekt: if + Aussagesatz, if the price includes …
wrong.en: “does” belongs in a direct question. Reported: if + statement order, if the price includes …

tasks.prompt: ___ the client's complaint while I was on vacation last week?

ok.de: Gefragt wird nach dem Handelnden (wer?). Bei der Subjektfrage fällt did weg: Who handled … „last week“?
ok.en: The question asks for the doer (who?). In a subject question there's no did: Who handled … “last week”?

wrong.de: „Who did handle“ klingt nach Betonung. Fragt who nach dem Subjekt, fällt did weg: Who handled.
wrong.en: “Who did handle” sounds emphatic. When who asks for the subject, drop did: Who handled.

wrong.de: „Whom“ fragt nach dem Objekt (wen?). Hier ist die Person das Subjekt: Who handled.
wrong.en: “Whom” asks for the object. Here the person is the subject: Who handled.

tasks.prompt: How often ___ the sales figures to the board these days?

ok.de: „How often … these days“ fragt nach einer Gewohnheit. Direkte Frage: do + Subjekt + Grundform.
ok.en: “How often … these days” asks about a habit. Direct question: do + subject + base form.

wrong.de: „did you send“ ist Vergangenheit. „these days“ fragt nach heute: do you send.
wrong.en: “did you send” is past. “these days” asks about now: do you send.

wrong.de: Es fehlt do. Deutsch sagt „Wie oft schickst du …?“ ohne Hilfsverb, Englisch braucht do: do you send.
wrong.en: do is missing. German needs no helper verb, but English does: do you send.

wrong.de: Nach do steht die Grundform ohne -s: do you send.
wrong.en: After do the verb has no -s: do you send.

tasks.prompt: We still haven't received their payment for the March invoice, ___?

ok.de: Der Satz ist verneint („haven't“). Das Anhängsel wird positiv, mit demselben Hilfsverb: have we.
ok.en: The statement is negative (“haven't”). The tag turns positive with the same auxiliary: have we.

wrong.de: Verneinter Satz, positives Anhängsel: „haven't … have we?“
wrong.en: Negative statement, positive tag: “haven't … have we?”

wrong.de: „isn't it“ ist kein Allzweck-Anhängsel wie „oder?“. Es wiederholt das Hilfsverb: have we.
wrong.en: “isn't it” is not an all-purpose tag like German “oder?”. Repeat the auxiliary: have we.

wrong.de: Das Hilfsverb im Satz ist have („haven't received“), also have we.
wrong.en: The auxiliary in the sentence is have (“haven't received”), so: have we.

tasks.prompt: Let's take a short break before the next session starts, ___?

ok.de: Nach „Let's“ ist das Anhängsel shall we.
ok.en: After “Let's” the tag is shall we.

wrong.de: „isn't it“ ist kein Allzweck-Anhängsel. Nach „Let's“ heißt es shall we.
wrong.en: “isn't it” is not an all-purpose tag. After “Let's” say shall we.

wrong.de: „don't we“ passt nicht zu „Let's“. Der Vorschlag bekommt shall we.
wrong.en: “don't we” doesn't fit “Let's”. The suggestion takes shall we.

tasks.prompt: Before I book my train, could you tell me ___ on Fridays?
options: what time does the office close
